newsitem.title: USA: Pixar reports nearly $10 million profit.
newsitem.headline: Pixar reports nearly $10 million profit.

text.p: Pixar Animation Studios, the computer animation firm that co-produced the hit film "Toy Story," Monday reported a $9.6 million profit for the third quarter.
The company said the profit was equal to 21 cents per share and compared with a net loss of $1.3 million, or 3 cents a share, for the third quarter of 1995.
Revenues rose to $13.8 million from $1.1 million.

Pixar also creates animated CD-ROMs and films, including Walt Disney Co.'s 1995 release "Toy Story." The company is deep into production of its second film, code-named "Bugs," and is starting work on its third film.
Net income for the first nine months of 1996 increased to $20.7 million, or 44 cents per share, from $3.1 million, or 8 cents a share a year earlier, the company said.
Revenues nearly tripled to $30 million from $10.6 million.
Pixar stock fell 12.5 cents to $16.625 on the Nasdaq.
